drhp.business: Lenskart designs and sells prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, contact lenses and eyewear accessories under its own brands and sub-brands through an omnichannel network of websites, mobile applications and 2,806 stores globally (2,137 in India, 669 international as of June 30, 2025). It runs a centralized supply chain with in-house frame and lens design and manufacturing at Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) and Gurugram (Haryana), supplemented by facilities in Singapore and the UAE.
drhp.certs: Bhiwadi facility operates as a zero liquid discharge manufacturing facility
drhp.end_markets: India (largest market; FY25 India segment revenue per Ind AS 108 approx 61% of segment revenue)|Japan, Southeast Asia and Middle East (international; International segment revenue 39.65% of external revenue FY25)
drhp.expansion: Deepen and broaden the India store network across Metropolitan, Tier 1 and Tier 2+ cities, funding approximately 620 new CoCo stores from Net Proceeds over FY2026 to November 2028; scale international operations (Japan, Southeast Asia, Middle East) leveraging India's centralized supply chain; a non-binding MoU dated December 8, 2024 with the Government of Telangana contemplates a greenfield manufacturing facility involving investment of approximately Rupees 15,000 million.
drhp.mdna: Product margin expansion via centralized procurement and in-house manufacturing (consolidated product margin 63.88% FY23 to 67.92% FY25)|EBITDA (excluding other income and exceptional item) margin improvement from 6.86% FY23 to 14.60% FY25 to 17.77% Q1FY26|International segment product margin lift post-Owndays (70.42% FY23 to 74.43% FY25)|High depreciation and amortisation and finance costs from leased store network (lease liabilities)|Inventory centralization (75.37% centralized as of March 31, 2025)

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Fully backward-integrated, centralized supply chain: in-house design of frames and lenses (since 2021), in-house frame and lens manufacturing (69.87% of prescription eyeglasses sold in FY25 made at India facilities; 6.44 million frames and 4.06 million lenses manufactured in FY25), centralized procurement of frames and lenses, lens coating/edging/cutting/polishing and assembly at Bhiwadi and Gurugram, supplemented by Singapore and UAE facilities. 75.37% of India inventory centralized at manufacturing facilities (March 31, 2025). Centralized model enables next-day delivery in 58 cities and 3-day delivery in 49 cities in India. India supply chain leveraged to serve international markets and Owndays post-acquisition.

market_position.basis: India's largest and fastest-growing eyewear company by revenue from operations (FY23-FY25) and largest seller of prescription eyeglasses by volume in India among organized retailers in FY25; in Asia amongst the two largest organized retailers of prescription eyeglasses by B2C eyeglasses sales volumes in FY25, per the Redseer Report. Brand spans economy to premium with 18.13% of India sales below Rupees 2,000 and 18.14% above Rupees 10,000 transaction value in FY25.

industry_peers.no_peer_note: There are no listed companies in India or globally which operate in a similar business model as ours.

opportunities: Low prescription eyeglasses penetration in India (~35%), SE Asia (~40%) and Middle East (~60%) vs US (~88%)
Shift from unorganised to organised retail (organised ~23% of India today)
TAM growth to ~Rupees 3,601 billion by FY2030 across India, SE Asia, Japan and Middle East
International expansion leveraging India supply chain (Owndays)
strengths: Centralized supply chain and 75%-automated Bhiwadi manufacturing (top-two vertically integrated eyewear facility globally by capacity)
In-house frame and lens engineering (69.87% of prescription eyeglasses sold in FY25 manufactured in-house)
Owned brand and sub-brand portfolio across price points; India's Most Trusted Eyewear Brand 2025 (TRA)
Technology-first omnichannel platform (2,806 stores, 100mn+ app downloads, AI try-on/computer vision/geo-analytics)
Highest store revenue per sq ft and largest India store footprint (~2.5x next leading organized retailer)
threats: Fragmented, largely unorganised competition constraining pricing power
Medical advances (LASIK/SMILE) potentially reducing eyewear demand
Import/tariff and geopolitical exposure to China
weaknesses: Only recently profitable (losses in FY23 and FY24)
All stores and offices leased; high depreciation and finance costs
Dependence on China imports for frames/raw materials

overview.business_model: Lenskart designs eyeglass frames and lenses in-house, manufactures them at centralized facilities in India (supplemented by Singapore and the UAE), and sells prescription eyeglasses, sunglasses, contact lenses and accessories directly to consumers under its own brands through an omnichannel network of websites, mobile applications and physical stores (CoCo, FoFo and CoFo formats). Revenue is driven by eyewear unit sales via transacting customer accounts, complemented by a paid Lenskart Gold loyalty membership.

employee_strength.note: 18,173 permanent employees and a contractual workforce of 5,812 (per risk factors); technology team of 491 members; 109-member design and merchandising team; 358 home try-on agents; 164 optometrists at central locations; employs personnel from 25 nationalities with 35.82% female employees, all as of June 30, 2025.

genesis.founding_story: Commenced operations in India as an online business in 2010 and opened its first retail store in New Delhi in 2013. Renamed Lenskart Solutions Private Limited in 2015 and converted to Lenskart Solutions Limited (public) in 2025.

concerns_observed: Only recently profitable: restated losses of Rupees 637.57 million (FY23) and Rupees 101.54 million (FY24), with negative investing/financing cash flows historically; FY25 RoNW is thin at 4.84%.
Fresh Issue is modest (Rupees 21,500 million) relative to a large Offer for Sale of up to 127,562,573 shares by PE/VC investors and Promoters, so most Offer proceeds do not accrue to the Company.

Low promoter holding at 19.83% of pre-Offer capital (fully diluted); a 9:1 bonus issue in October 2024 (within 18 months of the Offer) and weighted-average acquisition costs (Rupees 40.15 over three years, Rupees 55.93 over one year) well below the likely Offer Price.

Regulatory overhang: ongoing Enforcement Directorate inquiry under FEMA, denied ODI NOCs, a pending DPIIT Press Note 3 approval and RBI compounding application, plus auditor report modifications (audit trail/servers) across FY23-FY25.
Deployment risk on Net Proceeds: no definitive contracts/orders placed for CoCo store fit-outs, exact store locations not yet identified, and funding not appraised by any bank.

Supply-chain and cost exposure: raw materials ~24.52% of total expenses in FY25 (mostly spot-purchased); significant frame/raw-material import dependence on China including via the 51% Baofeng JV; low manufacturing capacity utilization (~55% total, Q1FY26).
No listed comparable peers disclosed, complicating relative valuation.
Outstanding litigation quantified at ~Rupees 1,943.6 million (approx 65% of FY25 PAT), including an FIR involving Promoter Peyush Bansal.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue CAGR 32.52% FY23-FY25 to Rupees 66,525.17 million; largest India organized prescription eyewear retailer by volume (Redseer).
EBITDA (excl OI) margin up to 14.60% (FY25) and turned PAT-positive (Rupees 2,973.40 million), but only recently profitable after FY23/FY24 losses; RoNW just 4.84%.
Net worth Rupees 61,082.99 million (FY25); modest borrowings (~Rupees 3,354.82 million) but historical negative cash flows and a covenant not met at Owndays for three years.
Vertically integrated centralized supply chain, top-two global manufacturing facility by capacity, largest India footprint (~2.5x next retailer), 79,000+ SKUs.
Experienced founder-led team (17+ years) and majority-independent board, but ED/FEMA inquiry, RBI compounding, auditor report modifications and low 19.83% promoter holding.

Detailed object-wise and year-wise deployment (stores, leases, technology, marketing), but CoCo store locations unidentified, no definitive orders, not bank-appraised, and a large unidentified inorganic/GCP bucket (up to 35% of Gross Proceeds).
No listed peer benchmark; P/E and price band left blank; large OFS by early investors; 9:1 bonus within 18 months; acquisition cost far below likely Offer Price.
India eyewear market ~13% CAGR to Rupees 1,483 billion by FY2030; low prescription-eyeglasses penetration (~35% India) and shift from unorganized (~77%) to organized retail.

red_flags: Ongoing Enforcement Directorate inquiry under FEMA with potential penalty up to thrice the sum involved, plus denied ODI NOCs.
Statutory Auditors' report modifications (audit trail/server backups; delayed statutory dues) across FY23-FY25.
9:1 bonus issue in October 2024 within 18 months of the Offer; weighted-average acquisition cost of Rupees 40.15 (three years) versus likely Offer Price.
FIR (October 26, 2024) involving Promoter Peyush Bansal and other senior personnel (stayed by Karnataka High Court, pending).
Net Proceeds not appraised by any bank; no definitive orders/contracts for CoCo store fit-outs and store locations unidentified.
strengths_observed: Largest organized retailer of prescription eyeglasses in India by volume and amongst the two largest in Asia by B2C eyeglasses sales volume (FY25, per Redseer), with the largest India store footprint (~2.5x the next leading organized retailer).

Fully backward-integrated centralized supply chain with 75%-automated Bhiwadi manufacturing (amongst top-two vertically integrated eyewear facilities globally by capacity); 69.87% of prescription eyeglasses sold in FY25 made in-house.
Strong revenue growth: revenue from operations grew from Rupees 37,880.28 million (FY23) to Rupees 66,525.17 million (FY25), a 32.52% CAGR.

Margin expansion: EBITDA (excl. other income and exceptional item) margin improved from 6.86% (FY23) to 14.60% (FY25) to 17.77% (Q1FY26); turned to restated PAT of Rupees 2,973.40 million in FY25 after prior-year losses.
Technology-led omnichannel model (2,806 stores, 100mn+ app downloads, AI virtual try-on, computer vision, geo-analytics) and high store productivity; new-CoCo-store average payback of 10.29 months.
Owned brand portfolio spanning economy to premium (Lenskart, John Jacobs, Owndays, Vincent Chase) with rising NPS (69.77 to 78.47 in India) and a 7.12 million-member Lenskart Gold base.
